reading.title: Poetry Under the Maple Tree
reading.purpose: Join fourth graders as they share original poems and songs at an outdoor school night.
paras: On Friday night, moms and dads brought quilts to the school yard for Poetry Night. Warm lamps hung from the maple limbs, and a small mic stood by the steps.

First up was Caleb. He spent all week working to compose a short poem about rain on a tin roof. He chose a haiku, a three-line poem with five, seven, and five beats. Because he had practiced each day, Caleb could recite it from mind without peeking at his card.

Next, Layla stepped up with a funny poem about a runaway shoe. Each verse, or group of lines, ended with a crisp rhyme like "street" and "feet." Her steady rhythm, a bouncy mix of strong and soft beats, made young kids tap their knees in time.

At the end, the fourth-grade band sang a song about spring. Mr. Lin played a sweet melody on his guitar, carrying the tune while singers shared poetic lines about green buds. When the chorus came back, the whole yard joined in.
When the last note died out, the crowd stood to applaud, clapping loud under the maple leaves.

choices: a repeating part of a song that everyone in the yard sings
a three-line poem with five, seven, and five beats
a funny story about a shoe running down a busy street
a gentle guitar tune played during a spring show

qs.q: Why did the younger children tap their knees during Layla's poem?
choices: Her poem had a bouncy rhythm that was easy to follow.
They were trying to keep warm on the blankets under the tree.
Mr. Lin asked them to play guitar beats during every funny poem.
Layla forgot her rhyme and asked the crowd to help her finish.
qs.why: Paragraph 3 says her steady, bouncy rhythm made little brothers and sisters tap their knees in time.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: How to hang paper lanterns safely from a tall maple tree at dusk
Students sharing original poems and a spring song at Poetry Night
Why a three-line haiku is harder to memorize than a funny poem
How Mr. Lin teaches guitar lessons to fourth graders every Friday
qs.why: The story describes Caleb, Layla, and the music group performing poems and a song for families in the courtyard.
